case.subject: Product meeting
case.title: Sprint planning: onboarding scope and owners

canvasName: R1-C02 Sprint planning: onboarding scope and owners

segments.text: Let's start the sprint planning meeting. We have a five person product team and two weeks. The goal for this sprint is to ship the new onboarding flow to a small group of beta users, not to finish everything on the backlog. Please keep that goal in mind when we discuss scope. I want us to leave with a committed set of stories, one owner for each, the dependencies, and the risks we accept. First, the business context.
segments.textReply: The board now captures the sprint length, team size, and goal: ship the onboarding flow to a small beta group—not finish the backlog.

segments.text: Last month only thirty eight percent of new users completed onboarding. The biggest drop off is at the workspace setup step, where people do not understand whether they need to invite their team right away. Support gets about twenty tickets a week about that screen.
segments.textReply: Added the business context: 38% onboarding completion, confusion at workspace setup, and about 20 related support tickets per week.

segments.text: The design team has three concepts: a shorter single page flow, a guided checklist that appears after signup, and an import workspace option for users who already have data. We cannot build all three in one sprint. The engineering capacity is sixteen developer days.
segments.textReply: Added the three competing concepts to the scope panel and noted the 16 developer-day capacity; no scope choice is recorded yet.

segments.text: Alex is on backend, Priya and Sam are on frontend, Diego is on infrastructure, and Mei is our designer who can pair on implementation but is only available four days. We also have one QA contractor for the second week. There is a company holiday next Friday, so the first week is four days and the second week is five, but QA cannot start before staging is stable. Here are the candidate stories.

segments.text: Story one, shorten the workspace setup page from four steps to two and remove the mandatory invite. That is about three frontend days and one backend day. Story two, add a progress checklist after signup. That is four frontend days, plus analytics, plus two backend days if we want to remember checklist state. Story three, import an existing workspace from a CSV.
segments.textReply: Added Stories 1 and 2. Story 1 is estimated at 3 frontend + 1 backend day; Story 2 at 4 frontend + 2 backend days if checklist state is persisted.

The design team recommends story one first.

shapes.title: Sprint planning summary
shapes.html:
Onboarding beta · Sprint plan
Two weeks · five-person product team · ship a focused, measurable onboarding improvement to a small beta group—not the full backlog.
CONSENSUS · COMMITTED SCOPE
  • Story 1: shorten workspace setup from 4 steps to 2; remove mandatory invite.
  • Story 5: fix invitation email bug; if no support repro by Wednesday, investigate only—do not count as shipped.
  • Story 4: capture 3 onboarding events; use a saved SQL view, no dashboard UI.
  • Import: Thursday week 1 technical design + migration prep only; no import UI.
  • Defer checklist one sprint; keep design ready and place it at top of next sprint backlog.
WHY THIS SCOPE

Only 38% complete onboarding; workspace setup is the main drop-off and drives ~20 support tickets/week. Story 1 directly addresses it. Three events keep the change measurable while protecting QA time.

Capacity guardrail: 16 developer days; reserve consent and mobile API commitments first.
Action items · owners and deadlines
WorkOwner(s)Deadline / checkpoint
